thread:
jonah: Anyone else seeing a token refresh loop in the Kotlin sample app on Android 12? App starts fine but after a bit background syncs keep getting 401 -> refresh -> 401 -> refresh.

maria: Hmm that's not great. Any logs you can paste?

jonah: Got a small snippet from logcat:
```
2025-04-16 09:12:34.123 com.sample D/Auth: refresh token success
2025-04-16 09:12:34.456 com.sample W/Sync: retrying after auth
2025-04-16 09:12:34.457 com.sample E/Network: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
```

kevin: Do you use an okhttp Authenticator or an Interceptor for refreshing? They behave differently when a request is retried.

jonah: Using okhttp3.Authenticator in the sample. Simplified code:
```
class TokenAuthenticator : Authenticator {
  override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
    val token = tokenProvider.refresh() // blocking
    return response.request.newBuilder()
      .header("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
      .build()
  }
}
```

lisa: Android 12 scheduling + blocking refresh can cause a pile-up of requests. If refresh blocks the network thread, multiple calls might trigger concurrent refreshes and clobber each other.

maria: Also double-check Retrofit suspend adapters — if you re-call the same Call it can re-enqueue and retrigger auth flow unexpectedly.

jonah: Repro steps I used: 1) run sampleapp branch auth-repro 2) point sampleapp at a MockWebServer 3) have server return 401 for refresh once then 200. Trigger Sync Now from settings -> observed ~4 refresh calls.

kevin: Common fix is to make refresh idempotent + dedupe concurrent refreshes. Use a mutex or single-threaded executor for refresh and have other requests wait for the single inflight refresh result.

maria: Another practical mitigation: small jittered backoff before attempting refresh, and if authenticate() sees that the request already has the new token header, return null to avoid retry loops.

sdk-bot: Ticket created: RDW-9342 by maria (labels: devex, sdk, p2) — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RDW-9342

lisa: I'll add a MockWebServer integration in sampleapp/tests/auth to assert only one refresh happens when refresh returns 200 after initial 401. Might add a comment about using Authenticator vs Interceptor.

kevin: Also note okhttp Dispatcher settings can matter — if maxRequestsPerHost is low and requests queue up, timing shifts. Worth checking for dispatcher saturation in the reproducer.

jonah: I'll open a PR with the repro branch and link the test. Quick link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/compare/auth-repro
